subject: Hosting mode scorecard and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosting mode scorecard and next steps

Team — attaching a lightweight scorecard (hosting_mode_scorecard_v2.xlsx) that consolidates latency, cost, throughput, data residency, and compliance risk across the three deployment modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) for CareGrid.

Quick asks:
- Can you scan columns B:E and flag anything you strongly disagree with (cost assumptions or SLOs) by EOD Wednesday?
- Priyom: please sanity-check the throughput numbers against the benchmark run last month (I pulled the 99P95 from the June run).
- Soojin: add a short note on SOC2 / data residency implications for EU in the comments column if you have a minute.

This is intended to be the customer-facing scorecard we'll walk through on a 30-min MAP review next week. The doc has a short executive summary on tab 1. I also drafted a 6-week MAP in the attached PDF (caregrid_map_draft.pdf) — want to keep the timeline tight to close this quarter.

Ben
Senior AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: hosting_mode_scorecard_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), caregrid_map_draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-06T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting mode scorecard and next steps

Ben — quick pass done. Two notes in-sheet:
- Cost model: our per-token cost for Dedicated is optimistic by ~12% for the 8k-seq baseline; suggest we add a conservative buffer column so we don't undercut pricing conversations.
- Latency: the 99th for Hosted in east-us is closer to 220ms not 180ms when under burst; I'll annotate with the June burst run.

Otherwise looks good. Happy to join the customer review if you want an engineering voice.

—Priyom

Hi Ellie — following up with the scorecard and draft MAP we discussed.

Attaching the scorecard and a one-page MAP draft for a short review. High level recommendation from our side (pending your constraints):
- US traffic: Dedicated pool in us-east for predictable latency and cost at scale.
- EU traffic: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem option) for data residency and auditability.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min scorecard review (I can walk through numbers) — can you share availability for next week?
2) We’ll update the MAP and produce a DocuSign-ready SOW for Dedicated + Private lanes once scope locked.
3) Draft a redline-friendly term sheet if you want procurement involved early.

Links: HubSpot record (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345) and a Drive copy of the scorecard (https://drive.google.com/file/d/scorecard-v2).

If that matches your expectation I’ll lock time and invite Soojin from Compliance to join.

Thanks,

Ben — thanks for the materials. A few quick clarifying questions before we schedule: 
1) For the EU traffic you recommend Private — does that imply an on-prem deployment at our Frankfurt cluster, or can it be a VPC-hosted private control plane in AWS eu-central?
2) For Dedicated in us-east, what kind of SLA and breach credit baseline are you assuming in the scorecard? Procurement will need those to start our internal approval.

We can do a 30-min call next Tue (14th) at 10:00 ET if that works.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ellie Park <ellie@caregrid.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting mode scorecard and next steps

Ellie — quick compliance note to answer your questions: 
- Private can be either: (a) VPC-hosted private control plane in AWS eu-central that maintains customer-managed networking and KMS integration, or (b) on-prem bundle if you require air-gapped. Both are supported; the scorecard assumes VPC-private for EU unless you explicitly request on-prem. I added a comment in the scorecard on the expected lead time (VPC-private ~4–6 weeks; on-prem ~8–12 weeks plus site validation).
- SLA assumptions for Dedicated: 99.9% uptime target, with standard breach credits (pro-rated monthly credits). I linked the SLA excerpt in the Drive copy (see HubSpot record). If CareGrid needs an enhanced SLA we can propose a premium commit.

If we lock VPC-private for EU and Dedicated in us-east for US, the MAP timeline on the draft PDF can hold — Priyom, can you confirm the throughput validation step (week 2) is feasible with the ops window Ellie mentioned?

—Soojin (Security & Compliance)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@caregrid.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Hosting mode scorecard and next steps — proposed path

Ellie — thanks for the quick replies. Based on Soojin's note and our internal pass, proposed path to finalize the MAP: 
1) Decision: Dedicated in us-east for US traffic; VPC-private in eu-central for EU traffic (CareGrid-managed VPC + KMS).
2) Week 1: Scorecard review call — confirm final cost buckets and SLA baseline (30 min).
3) Week 2: Throughput validation run (Priyom to run targeted burst tests with your ops team; ~4 hours of joint testing).
4) Week 3–4: Draft SOW & DocuSign (I’ll circulate redline-friendly SOW and term sheet for procurement).
5) Week 6: Target cutover for Dedicated lane; Private EU follow-on cutover aligned to validation and audit evidence.

Proposed times for the scorecard call: Tue 2026-07-14 10:00 ET or Wed 2026-07-15 09:00 ET. Please pick one and I’ll lock it.

Related links: HubSpot (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345), Drive scorecard (https://drive.google.com/file/d/scorecard-v2), DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/rdw/CareGrid-MAP).

If CareGrid confirms the VPC-private path for EU, I will: (a) add Soojin to the procurement thread, (b) produce an SOW draft for Dedicated + Private lanes, and (c) open a deal task in HubSpot with the MAP milestones.

Thanks — look forward to locking next week.

Ben Carter
